Spacecoin's Parent Company Signs $50M Binding Pre-Order Deal for Freeport Satellite Services in the Philippines Space Network, the space infrastructure company behind Spacecoin, has signed a $50 million binding pre-order agreement with HQ Company to bring satellite connectiity to the Philippines. Under the agreement, Space Network will provide Freeport network access, hardware, software and engineering support, while HQ Company will handle local sales, customer acquisition, spectrum authorizations and operations. Space Network plans to grow their constellation from the current four LEO satellites in orbit to approximately 230 satellites by 2029 and begin commercial services. The agreement follows Space Network's $100 million deal with Vietnam's DETI Technology in June 2026. Together, the two bring its commercial pre-orders to $150 million in only four months. Sponsored by Spacecoin — link

Cboe Extends Exclusive S&P 500 Index Options License Through 2051, Explores Tokenized Options Contracts Cboe Global Markets announced a 25-year extension of its exclusive licensing agreement with S&P Dow Jones Indices through 2051. Under the agreement, Cboe will retain exclusive rights to offer trading in its flagship S&P 500 Index (SPX) options, while the two companies may also explore new products beyond traditional index derivatives, including tokenized options contracts. SPX options reached a record 970.6 million contracts in 2025, with average daily volume of 3.9 million contracts, up 25% year over year. No specific tokenized options product or launch timeline has been announced. — link

Kalshi Seeks $1 Billion at $40 Billion Valuation as Sequoia, Wellington, Tiger Global and Dragoneer Circle Round Reuters reported that prediction market platform Kalshi is in advanced talks to raise about $1 billion from existing and new investors, including Tiger Global and Dragoneer. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks at a valuation of about $40 billion, up roughly 82% from the $22 billion valuation in its $1 billion May financing. Existing investor Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management are in talks to lead the round. Kalshi has also held early discussions about a potential IPO in the coming years. Polymarket is separately seeking about $1 billion in new funding. — link

OpenAI Seeks at Least $30 Billion at $1.4 Trillion Pre-Money Valuation Bloomberg reported that OpenAI is seeking at least $30 billion in new funding at a pre-money valuation of about $1.4 trillion. The talks remain at an early stage and terms could change. The round is intended as bridge financing after OpenAI postponed its IPO plans. The company has confidentially filed to go public, but CEO Sam Altman said it will not pursue an IPO this year. OpenAI last raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation. If completed at the targeted valuation, the new round would put OpenAI’s private-market valuation back above Anthropic’s. — link
